newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen a bit higher due to fall in stocks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen a bit higher due to fall in stocks.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract was slightly higher by midday on Thursday, due to a sharp fall in Tokyo share prices and the yen's strength against the dollar, traders said.

"December was sold initially, but it was later bought back as the yen strengthened against the dollar, share prices fell below the key 20,000 level and Japanese government bonds rose sharply," said a city bank trader.
December stood at 98.93 by midday, up slightly from the previous day's settlement of 98.92.
The morning session's turnover was 47,112 contracts.
December's upside is likely to be limited, however, as the market remains concerned about a possible rise in interest rates, the city bank trader said.
"The current level of around 98.93 is a comfortable place for the December. I think it will move in a range centered around 98.90 for the time being," the trader said.
December was sold at the open as Tokyo share prices initially remained above the key 20,000 level despite the yen's rise versus the dollar, said a trader for another city bank.
But short-covering needs at below 98.90 helped boost the December after the early falls, the trader said.
